title: Holocene shoreline and river history of the Susiana plain: which watercourse is the Eulaios, and where lay the Persian Gulf coast in 1158, 647 and 474 BCE?
question: What do peer-reviewed geoarchaeological studies, borehole and coring records, and published palaeogeographic maps establish about the Holocene evolution of the Susiana plain and the head of the Persian Gulf: the position of the coastline around 8000, 5500 and 2500 years BP, the avulsion history of the Karun, Karche/Schaur and Dez, and the identification of the ancient Eulaios? Which of these lines can be drawn for the Chronomap epochs 1158, 647 and 474 BCE with [R] (mapped or cored) versus [S] (inferred) status? Specifically: is the current equation Eulaios = Karche/Schaur (Potts 1999) defensible against the alternative that the Eulaios is the Dez or another arm; what does Heyvaert & Baeteman (Marine Geology 242, 2007), Fig. 11a-g actually show for each epoch; and what do the irrigation-channel and settlement records imply about which channels existed in each period?
why_now: On 24.11.2026 the Susiana map base was drawn with land and a schematic Karche, but the Gulf coast after Heyvaert & Baeteman Fig. 11 is explicitly still undrawn, the Dez and the exact Schaur are unresolved, and the Madaktu/Badake location depends on the Eulaios identification (docs/world/chronomap-erde/warteschlange.md, same day; docs/world/chronomap-erde/wissen/landschaft-im-wandel.md, section 2).
real_world_anchor: Holocene sea-level, delta and fluvial-avulsion history of the Susiana plain and the Persian Gulf head (Heyvaert & Baeteman 2007 and later geoarchaeological coring), plus the identification of the ancient Eulaios/Karche river.
novelty_reason: No previous topic covers Susiana, Elam or the Persian Gulf. The Galilee site-and-road topic concerns a different region, period and evidence base (first-century CE Lower Galilee), and the Passion-chronology topic concerns astronomy rather than Holocene geomorphology.
